city-digital-twin · Newcastle study · project report

Built, unrun, and a stall nobody killed

2026-09-11HEAD 20ae4e9branch praneetdhoolia/project-report-and-fixesgate PASS (18/18)

The state is unchanged since the last report and the reason is now precise. The only result the project has (20260909T015217_300it_25pct, F32, iteration 300) reads 0 of 12 modes inside 10 %; the F33 family that would test the demand fix has no reading, because its first arm ran 20.9 hours on a 14 GB heap that the registry's own rule forbade and nothing evaluated, spent 13.1 of those hours stalled inside iteration 89 with the machine awake, and died of OutOfMemoryError at iteration 98. The previous six reports were followed to an unusual degree — 76 of 105 recommendations taken, the median within a day — and the goal count did not move, because what was taken was instruments (the objective, the gate, the pricer, the coverage reader, the count-station map) and every model-side control those instruments produced is built and unrun: score MSA at the cutoff, random plan removal, the raptor mode constant, service quality, pt submodes, and the passenger placed on ride. The code carries 6 new defects, one of which (build_matsim_network.py:137) means the package has not been regenerable from raw since 25 August with every gate green, and one (EscortCoherenceListener.trim) that makes one of the five paired controls partly unreachable; one bootstrap and two consolidations would remove 4,000–5,500 lines with every behaviour kept. The record works; the position pages have become a second unpruned log (37 contradictions, 18 carried). What stands between the project and its first calibrated reading is no longer knowledge or tooling — it is six paired arms of about 19 hours each, and the launch discipline that lost 21 hours yesterday.

Method

Eighth report of the series, the first rendered by render_report.py from the lanes' JSON rather than written by hand. Six lanes ran in parallel after the three collectors: one code reviewer over six areas (28,285 of 91,483 lines in scope read completely, the rest queried; every unread file with a metrics row is named per area), one performance analyst over 173 runs' own stopwatches and the two newest arms' logs, one historian over all 68 PRs and the six previous reports' 105 recommendations, one document reviewer over every living and archived document, hook, workflow and skill plus the whole issue ledger, and two researchers at the full 40-call budget each (the user's choice this pass) over the reference library's gaps and this pass's per-mode data question. Ten cited file:lines and the two sharpest lane findings were re-read by the writer (appendix). Ratings are 1–5 per area per dimension, each carrying two pieces of evidence; they are never averaged. Nothing under src/, cities/, the registry or the living documents was changed by this report; the reference library and the skill's renderer are the only writes.

The timeline from day 0

  • Day 0 (10 Aug): the proposal, the data package, the network and the demand landed in one day as PRs #1-#3; P4 began the next morning when none of the 30 run-input sets would load (#4).
  • Days 1-6: the registry, zero hardcoding and the cities/<city> split were built while the model was found to be running on a harvest box that clipped 87 SA1s; the rebuild of 15-16 Aug (#38) made everything before it incomparable and the family ledger starts there (F1).
  • Days 8-11 (18-21 Aug): ride pairing, escort binding, freight, motorbike, physical walk/bike and the first 34.7 h arm (#40-#64); a six-PR stack stranded on 20 Aug and the direct-commit ban followed on 21 Aug.
  • Days 14-15 (24-25 Aug): the two 67 h F4 arms completed and C5 was written from them - still the front door's fit figures; the same two days renamed the project, descoped SUMO and activated signals, crossings, dwell and taxi (F6).
  • Days 16-20 (26-30 Aug): the gate loop, thirteen sessions and 64 record rows in one week; 30 Aug alone opened F14-F21 and wrote 31 §14 rows; the documents were restructured onto one page (#101) and the demand rebuilt on measured licence rates.
  • Days 21-24 (31 Aug-3 Sep): fares, behaviour channels, the results store, the 25 %-only directive, the issue gate; bus was the first mode inside at a gate (1 Sep) and no mode held.
  • Days 24-27 (3-6 Sep): the first whole-repository report and its 14 defects closed the same day; destinations balanced at both ends; the iteration profiled (60 % ride pairing) and halved; a stopped run became citable.
  • Days 28-29 (7-8 Sep): four reports in 36 hours; car inside at the F28 gate (+6.6 %); F27-F31 opened; the iteration cut to 205 s and the arm to ~20 h; the objective restated onto the twelve modes and the search made runnable.
  • Day 30 (9 Sep): the first arm since 21 Aug to run its horizon - and relaxing made the fit worse (0 of 12 at 300, car snapping +2.211 pp at the cutoff).
  • Day 31 (10 Sep): the count rung found orphaned for 25 days and repaired (+16.3 % not −89 %); the choice-set ceiling read (ride's target above its coverage); every MATSim default declared; F33 rebuilt with the passenger on ride.
  • Day 32 (11 Sep): F33's baseline arm died at iteration 98 on a 14 GB heap its overlay failed to raise; no approval stands; five one-field controls are built and none has a paired reading.
  • Across 32 days: 520 commits, 66 merged PRs, 131 record sections, 33 families, 173 run directories, 426.9 machine hours, one result, zero modes inside 10 % at it.

Three questions

a
PER LAUNCH (once per arm): run.py -> issue_gate.refuse_launch (one gh issue list, twice under --detach) -> registry.load (8 JSON files + 356-field validation) -> run_matsim.run: reconcile_stale (every _meta.json + a 64 MiB log-tail read per dead-but-running card), results_store.migrate, announce_cost (every _run.json/_progress.json on disk), controler_sha256 (59 Java files), values_sha256, inputs_sha256 (the 78 MB plans gz), find_completed (every record), build_config -> subsample_plans (two full streams of the plans gz: lift_cluster_map then the sample) + scale_transit_capacity + scoring_from_c1 + write_mode_vehicles + param_config.emit, write_snapshot, then the JVM. PER ITERATION while the JVM runs (Python side): progress_digest every RUN.monitor.progress_interval_s (run_view.scan + the incremental log reader), the live view on demand, the gate watcher every 30 s (_last_ended_iteration = one JSON read) and at every RUN.gate.interval_iterations milestone a full report_mode_ridership.py subprocess (registry load, targets, trips table x2, legs, experienced plans/legs, schedule, config), the ceiling watcher every RUN.gate.ceiling_poll_s, and _trim_async once after launch (an os.walk of results/raw plus up to two reporter subprocesses per over-cap directory). Everything else per iteration is Java: RidePairingEngine.notifyBeforeMobsim (every selected plan, parallel detours), EscortCoherenceListener.notifyReplanning (every household during innovation), HouseholdVehicleRoster.notifyIterationStarts (every person), GatedSubtourModeChoice per replanned plan, the six scorers per event and at AfterMobsim, RunTelemetry per event. PER RUN END: iteration_times (digest, else a full log walk), close_out/summarise_run (one full output_events.xml.gz stream on a run that has one), results_store.process (two reporter subprocesses: --trend over EVERY readable iteration = N x report(), then --json), trim, extract_metrics (output_trips x4, output_legs x2, output_links, schedule), mirror. ONCE PER BUILD: every module under src/build/, cities/<city>/build/ and cities/<city>/extract/, build_manifest, normalise_eol; and build_matsim_run_inputs.main (not its emitter) - the run imports the module but never main().
b
SILENT (a bug changes a number nobody sees move): the four-pass binders and the plans writer (a wrong seed, an off-by-one trip index in boundRideTrips - no test, no contract, the plans file is hashed but not checked against anything); patch_link's except: pass (:764-774) turning a variant partial; through_gates' uncounted continues; a build-time field set in a run overlay (records it as moved, executes the base); write_parking_prices at base resolution; EscortCoherenceListener.trim ignoring the declared selector; PtCrowdingScoring discarding aboard-at-end; RunTelemetry/RidePairingEngine handler state published by a config flag; _trip_cell mapping any text to 50; report_mode_ridership's substring station match; build_status_board's literal 20%/10% headers after a threshold sweep; the three skipped_large manifest rows; registry_overrides: {} on every record; the ceiling marker's BEGUN iteration in the cause text; the stale counts in WEEKDAY.json; run_view calling a stopped arm failed; _metrics.json/_fit.json written past their contracts. LOUD (a bug stops the pipeline and names itself): the resolver (unknown field, out-of-sweep, held-fixed, unobtained, missing overlay, derived_from integrity, sweep roles); param_config.closure and collect's double-write refusal; check_scoring_order; split_schedule's stray transport modes; patch_signal_capacities and check_change_event_links on a foreign build; the binders' contiguity assertion; refuse_if_no_automatic_stop, refuse_unsafe_telemetry, the parking-price and signal-regime checks in build_config; outputs.write_checked on _meta/_run/_summary; fit.py's reconciliation; calibrate.objective's missing-component refusal; check_registry_rules; HouseholdVehicleRoster's missing car type; GatedSubtourModeChoice re-throwing the subtour mix with the plan printed; tc.require()'s arity error (loud, and the wrong message: ValueError rather than "the network build is broken"). The dividing line at HEAD: anything that reaches _run.json, _meta.json, the config text or a registry value is loud; anything that lives in a plan file, a per-iteration table, a handler's map or a description string is silent.
c
1. ONE BOOTSTRAP. Make src/ an importable package (pyproject.toml, pip install -e ., or a single .pth) and give builders a @citysim.build.main decorator that starts the timing clock and resolves the registry lazily: removes the 238 sys.path lines in 122 files, the 36 pasted "City-relative paths" preambles (~180 lines), the 31 pasted build_timing blocks (~310 lines) and the 26 import-time registry.load() calls - 650-900 lines, every behaviour kept, touches a result: none. 2. FIELD-LEVEL CONFIG GROUPS. Rewrite the 18 ReflectiveConfigGroups (3,336 lines, ~140 @StringGetter/@StringSetter pairs) as public @Parameter-annotated fields, keeping every checkConsistency, and fold the seven pasted "one instance in two roles" modules in CitysimControler.assemble into one helper: 2,100-2,700 lines, byte-identical emitted config (verify on a smoke run's output_config.xml), touches a result: none. 3. ONE READER AND ONE BINDER. Give src/analyse/ an IterationReading that streams trips, legs and plans once and serves report(), extract_metrics, measure_iteration_modes, iteration_trips, summarise_run and the four duplicate measurement pairs (800-1,200 lines, none of it result-bearing beyond byte-equal _metrics.json); and give build_activity_chains one Binder over which the escort, lift, joint and shared passes are three rule sets (400-550 lines, unknown until run - the binding order must reproduce the committed WEEKDAY tables exactly, which the manifest hashes prove or refute). Together: roughly 4,000-5,500 of the areas' ~72,000 lines, of which only the binder consolidation can move a result and it is verifiable before any arm.

architecture
The build layer is a linear pipeline from immutable downloads to run inputs: build_network_layers (OSM -> A1/A6/A2/A5) -> attach_gradient/attach_speed_zones (in-place) -> build_matsim_network (pt2matsim, once per comparison) -> build_zone_attractions -> build_population (B1) -> build_activity_chains (B2: tours, decays, four binder passes, three boundary tiers) -> build_matsim_plans (population_<DAY>.xml.gz, the full-choice-set seed) -> build_matsim_run_inputs (per scenario x day: schedule filter, network patches, parking prices, C1 -> MATSim scoring, the config through param_config) -> build_manifest. Every value is read from cities/<city>/registry/ through the resolver, most at import (26 modules). The city's own builders (cities/newcastle/build/, 15 scripts) produce the targets, the corridor, the signals data and the scenario schedules. Nothing here runs per iteration; build_matsim_run_inputs is imported at every launch for scoring_from_c1, write_mode_vehicles and write_config.
testability
None of the eight demand/network builders is imported by a unit test; tests/check_package.py (workstation only) is the whole verification. Each builder takes 20-90 minutes on the full package, so a fixture path (--max-persons, --max-sa1) exists but no test uses it. The crash at build_matsim_network.py:137 is the measurement of this: a one-line arity error survived 17 days and every CI run.

architecture
run.py is the front door; run_matsim.run owns identity (three hashes + parameters), the nested household sample, the config emission through the builder's own emitter, the JVM launch, five daemons (live view, digest, trim, gate watcher, ceiling watcher) and four terminal boundaries (ran_to_last_iteration, stopped_at_gate, stopped_at_ceiling, stopped_by_operator), each closed out into a record the output contract checks. results_store owns every path under results/; issue_gate asks GitHub before a launch; run_failure reads a cause out of the log tail; session_gate runs the 18 gates. Overlays resolve through registry.load in scenario -> day -> run -> env -> set order. The harness is Windows-first (Task Scheduler detach, taskkill, kernel handles) with POSIX branches in the harness but not in the bootstrap.
testability
12 of 33 unit files import run_matsim; check_gate_watcher.py and check_launch_refusal.py drive the stop and refusal paths against fakes; test_find_completed, test_close_out, test_stop_run, test_ceiling_watch, test_trim_grace cover resume, close-out, stop, ceiling and trim. Untested: sample_population (the nested hash sample every arm depends on), run_failure.from_log, session_gate, verify_launch, prune_run, run_signal_probes, and the --detach path (Task Scheduler) by construction.

architecture
Two families of reader. Per-iteration: report_mode_ridership.report() (the twelve-mode reading) over measure_iteration_modes.trip_rows, iteration_trips (derived trips and boardings from experienced plans) and extract_metrics's schedule index; it feeds the gate (--gate-json), the store snapshots (--trend, --json), the board and the calibration objective (fit.score_goal_modes). Per finished run: extract_metrics -> _metrics.json -> fit.py -> _fit.json -> calibrate.py / build_fit_figures / report.py. Around them, 17 single-question measurement scripts, the live view (run_view + progress_digest, one incremental log reader shared with the gate), the run index and the board generator. The reading point is a point reading everywhere but the stability measurement, which DECISIONS.md 9.159 established is the right call.
testability
fit.py (26 tests), calibrate.py (13 + 6 + 4), arm_cost (4 + 4), compare_runs (9), build_fit_figures (7), report_choice_set_coverage (7), extract_metrics.iteration_stem (4) are covered. report_mode_ridership.py - the reader every result passes through - is not, nor is any of the 17 measurement scripts; a 20-trip fake ITERS/it.N directory would test the reader in under a second.

architecture
src/registry/__init__.py is the one resolver: eight registry files, intrinsic rules (sweep required by source, values inside sweeps, sweep roles, derived_from integrity), JSON Schema when available, five layers, a snapshot. param_config builds tool configs from matsim_param bindings and proves reach by nudging. check_hardcoding asks five questions (unwired, report-only, template literal, decided constant, coordinate) with a written exemption ledger; check_matsim_defaults asks the sixth (what the framework decides). outputs holds seven output contracts. tests/ holds ten check scripts (manifest, package, doc currency, doc shape, city-agnostic, gate watcher, launch refusal, registry rules, requirements) and 33 unit files; CI runs everything that needs only committed files on Python 3.14. The city owns its rules (cities/newcastle/tests/doc_currency.json, doc_shape.json, package_expectations.json) and its 356 declared fields.
testability
The registry (test_param_config, test_inert_at, test_outputs, check_registry_rules) and the doc gates are well covered; check_package.py is untestable as written (2,100 lines of module-level statements). Six tests assert Java by regex over source with comments stripped - they pass on a behaviour change that keeps the text.

architecture
cities/newcastle/extract/ holds the jurisdiction-specific adapters: five downloaders (ABS census/DEM, TfNSW open data and GTFS, licences) that write provenance_*.json beside the bytes, an Overpass harvester over derived extents, six extracts that turn published tables into the processed layers, and reader_shapes.py, the adapter through which the framework reads census and HTS shapes. The manifest (512 rows: 92 raw, 420 processed; 279 CC-BY, 218 ODbL; 0 undetermined lineage) records hash, rows, producer, source, licence and retrieval per row, with lineage resolved per output. The validation targets carry the pre-registered 67/143 split; the per-mode targets are a second, finer view the builder deliberately keeps out of that file.
testability
No adapter or extract script is exercised by any test; the layer is verified only by re-running it against the live sources and comparing manifest hashes. A recorded HTTP fixture per adapter would make the provenance writers testable offline.

architecture
CitysimControler.assemble is the stock Controler plus 19 typed config groups and a gate per mechanism: mode availability (AvailabilityModesCalculator, GatedSubtourModeChoice), ride pairing and physical boarding (RidePairingEngine, JointRideEngine, EscortCoherenceListener, RemodeRestore), the household car roster and its departure handler, a finite taxi fleet, network walk/bike with capped and gradient-aware speeds (CappedSpeedTravelTime, GradientLinkSpeed, GenericRouteTeleporter, TolerantAgentSource), the PT router extensions (NetworkDirectWalkPtRouter, SubmodeRaptorProvider, RaptorModeCostCalculator, PtSubmodeMainModeIdentifier), six deferred-emission scorers/chargers (parking, PT fare, taxi flagfall, bike stress, crowding, service quality), income scaling through MATSim core's IndividualPersonScoringParameters, and RunTelemetry. src/java_signals/ adds the signals-contrib entry point, the SCATS and tram-priority controllers and a gradient-aware signals network factory, compiled against the Maven run stack. Every class states the DECISIONS section it lives in and the byte-identical model its off value recovers.
testability
No Java test harness (the pinned toolchain carries none; adding JUnit is a DECISIONS.md 14 toolchain change). Six main-method probes cover SCATS, tram priority, the assembly, the restore, the gated strategy and the fare lookup; RidePairingEngine, EscortCoherenceListener, RunTelemetry, HouseholdVehicleRoster, JointRideEngine, TaxiFleetEngine, the six scoring handlers and TolerantAgentSource have no probe.

Verdict on the 250-iteration horizon

The 250-iteration horizon is reachable and was: the landed arm executed 300 iterations in 21.5 h at a 244 s median (254.5 s mean with milestones), so 250 is ~17.9 h, one overnight arm, and the pace is stable across F30-F33 bytecode on 40g (239-261 s) with its variance in the mobsim, not in anything of ours (our listeners are ~2% of a plain iteration). Nothing on the table halves it: the mobsim is 78% of the iteration and its measured levers are spent (threads 16, events 4, PassingQ on correctness); the only two-fold cuts are the fraction (10%, refused on model grounds) and the horizon itself (innovation to 0.9 with 250 declared buys the same search for ~30% less wall). What this pass adds is that the binding constraint on 10 September was heap, not time - the first OutOfMemory in 173 runs, costing 20.9 h of machine (6.5 h of iterations plus a 13 h wedge the record does not carry) for a reason the registry had written down and the launcher never read; the three zero-per-iteration changes at the top (evaluate the heap rule, kill a wedged JVM, checkpoints at +1.4-1.9%) recover more machine-hours than every per-iteration repair left, because 40.4% of all 426.9 machine-hours to date (172.6 h aborted or failed) still bought no citable reading.

ours

name
city-digital-twin - Newcastle (NSW) study (this repository)
engine
MATSim end to end, with project-owned Java extensions (src/java/citysim, src/java_signals) for signals, ride pairing and mode-specific constraints
city_population
Newcastle (NSW) region - five LGAs, 1,500 core SA1s, base year 2026
sample_fraction
25% (standing directive since 1 Sep 2026). The result run: 154,347 persons kept, 16 threads, xmx 40 g, median iteration 244.05 s, wall 77,309 s for 300 iterations; peak heap 36,243 MB (section 9.165). The F33 arm on 14 g died at 98 - a 4-iteration pricing probe prices time and cannot price heap, which grows with plan memory over the first hundred iterations.
modes
TWELVE, each scored individually: car, ride, walk, taxi, bike, motorbike, bus, heavy_rail, light_rail, ferry, truck, freight_train
active_modes
physical - walk and bike are simulated on the network, not teleported (positions/walk-and-bike.md)
pt_physical
yes - bus, heavy rail, light rail and ferry run the mapped GTFS schedule on the mapped network; 15 feeds mapped, 0 unmapped stops
signals
yes - SCATS implemented as its published algorithm (registry A.signals.scats.*: target degree of saturation, cycle bounds, ds smoothing/deadband, cycle step) plus transit signal priority (A.signals.tsp.*)
freight
yes - truck as a road vehicle scored on network-wide road-vehicle share; freight rail as timetable-derived level-crossing closures rather than a mobsim vehicle
fares_pricing
yes - Opal fare schedule in the registry (A.fare.*: peak/off-peak by mode, child/senior classes, daily and weekend caps, distance bands) plus priced parking (A.parking.*: charged hours, modes, price percentiles, search time) and a monetary distance rate (C.scoring.monetary_distance_rate)
validation_rung
per-mode ridership, every simulated mode - the top rung, and still the only project in this survey of 50 attempting it for twelve modes. The pass of 9 September qualified the claim (a four-step model, WFTDM, does report six transit modes inside 10%); THIS pass qualifies it further and more precisely: the WFRC ActivitySim framework's own Table 29 lists 'Transit boardings by transit mode' as a standard validation summary, so per-transit-mode granularity is normal agency practice for an activity-based model. What no other row does is treat every one of twelve modes as a SCORED TARGET WITH A BAND that the calibration is obliged to satisfy simultaneously.
best_fit
In calibration, no mode inside 10% at the newest result. 20260909T015217_300it_25pct, family F32, 25%, 300 of 300 iterations, 21.5 h (77,309 s), ran_to_last_iteration, is_a_result: true: 0 OF 12 INSIDE 10%, eight past the 20% stop bar - car +11.3%, motorbike +12.5%, ride -41.0%, walk -26.5%, taxi +202.2%, bike +113.0%, bus +44.8%, heavy_rail +225.0% (21,220 vs 6,529 boardings), light_rail -57.3% (1,260 vs 2,954), ferry -60.1%; truck level-only, freight_train representation-only. _fit.json on all four families at once: 5 scored mode-share targets mean absolute 4.734 pp; 30 count stations mean absolute 91.69% with 7 modelled zeros, median -98.75%; occupancy 0.1860 vs 0.3503; trip geometry outside range on all five reported modes (walk 3.283 km vs 0.7). The F33 dead arm's iteration-90 reading (car +0.9%, walk -2.7%, motorbike -4.5% inside; seven modes past the bar) is citable at 90 and nowhere past it, and is not a result.
open_source
yes - the repository; OSM-derived layers ODbL 1.0, the rest CC-BY 4.0
reproducible
yes and gated - every derived file regenerable by a committed script from immutable hashed raw downloads, 512 files in data/MANIFEST.csv with hash, rows, producing script, source, licence and retrieval date; everything synthetic seeded (20260810)
city_agnostic
yes by construction - src/, config/schema/, tests/ and run.py must read identically for an unseen city; all 480 registry fields, adapters and geometry live under cities/<city>/, enforced by check_city_agnostic.py and check_hardcoding.py --strict at 0
status
active, in calibration - P4 at HEAD 20ae4e9 (PR #179 merge, 11 Sep 2026). Registry 514 fields, manifest 512 files (279 CC-BY / 218 ODbL / 15 bespoke), 30 assembled run-input sets, 173 run directories on disk. Family F33-the-passenger-is-put-on-ride is open and HAS NO READING: its first 25% arm, aborted_20260910T222830_300it_25pct, died of OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space in the replanning of iteration 98 after 97 completed iterations and 6.5 h, on the registry's 14 g heap because the overlay copied the landed arm's horizon and not its 40 g (positions/runs-and-economics.md, section 9.165); write_plans_interval = 100 left checkpoints at it.0 and it.1 only, so nothing can be warm-started and the 6.5 h is lost. The board's scoreboard block currently reads the dead arm at iteration 90 and says so - it is NOT a result. The newest RESULT is unchanged: 20260909T015217_300it_25pct.
does_best
Every controllable value declared with units, provenance and a sweep or held-fixed rule (497 fields), every living number pinned to its artefact by a check, twelve modes each monitored on its own basis every tenth iteration - and, unique in this survey, a REGISTRY-ENFORCED refusal to fit a constant over a named missing mechanism (C.asc.rail's departure_requires clause). THIS PASS ADDS A SECOND UNIQUENESS, AND IT IS THE HONEST ONE: the project's _fit.json scores mode shares, absolute link counts, trip-length geometry and vehicle occupancy IN ONE ARTEFACT FROM ONE RUN, names its 32 unscorable targets with reasons, and refuses to call a stopped arm a result. Across 50 surveyed projects, the closest published analogues each hold part of that - AToM validates five observation families but calibrates against one; Tallinn optimises three target families at once but reports no per-mode transit rung; the WFRC framework enumerates every validation summary but states outright that not all of them can be met simultaneously.

calibration_method
family
coordinate descent over registry-declared sweeps (unchanged, never run to completion) PLUS, NEW AT THIS HEAD AND NEVER RUN, an implemented ASC log-ratio fixed point - src/calibrate/asc_fixed_point.py. Read from the source at HEAD 781cf41, not searched.
what_the_source_says
src/calibrate/calibrate.py:508-533 runs coordinate descent: per round, per free parameter, per grid point across that parameter's registry sweep, a FULL MATSim run -> extract_metrics -> fit -> a weighted scalar objective over declared _fit.json components, keeping a point only if it is feasible against the C4 occupancy and trip-length constraints; the round stops when the improvement falls below delta. The search space is DERIVED FROM THE REGISTRY, not listed in the script: a field is free only if it is source=assumed, carries a scalar sweep and is not held_fixed. The six mode constants are held_fixed under DECISIONS.md 8.5 and are therefore unreachable from the loop by construction - so this project has NO log(target/modelled) ASC loop of any kind. The one constant that is solved, asc_car_passenger, is solved in a separate module (solve_asc_ride.py:101-121) by SECANT INTERPOLATION ON log(ride_per_car) against the observed passenger:driver ratio, and is reported as a CONSTRAINT, not an estimate. The loop refuses to fit more parameters than the objective identifies (four independent numbers) and cannot read a holdout row by construction.
objective_evaluations
coordinate descent: calibrate.py:433 computes the budget as sum(len(grid(p, points_per_param)) for p in free) * max_rounds FULL MATSim runs; at 25% an arm reaching iteration 100 cost 7.66 h wall, so a 3-point 3-parameter 2-round search is ~18 arms and ~140 machine hours. THE LOOP HAS NEVER BEEN RUN TO COMPLETION. The ASC fixed point is far cheaper by design - TWO arms settle the contraction question - and is the only one of the two that has an evaluation count small enough to state in advance. Neither has been executed.
convergence_criterion
round-over-round objective improvement < delta

asc_fixed_point_new_this_pass
src/calibrate/asc_fixed_point.py EXISTS and PROPOSES ONLY; it has NEVER BEEN RUN. It applies delta_i = damping * [ ln(target_i/modelled_i) - ln(target_ref/modelled_ref) ] against car as reference - the same object as the Berry (1994) share inversion and the same expression matsim-vsp/matsim-python-tools computes verbatim, with the damping declared on CAL.asc.damping. THREE DESIGN CHOICES ARE UNUSUAL AND WORTH RECORDING: (1) THE TEST IS THE CONTRACTION, NOT THE SHARES - two damped rounds are compared mode by mode, and if |delta| shrinks the residual is a taste that constants will close, while if it does not shrink the deficit is STRUCTURAL and no constant will ever close it. That is a cheap, decisive, published-in-spirit answer to the 'constant or mechanism' question that the agency protocol answers only by ordering. (2) It CANNOT REACH A FROZEN CONSTANT: it reads held_fixed from the registry and refuses, structurally, the way the holdout guard refuses. (3) On heavy rail and light rail the step is marked basis_is_boardings and reported as a PROXY, because the logit inversion is exact only for shares of a common total. ROUND 1 IS PROPOSED OFF THE F31 GATE AND NOT APPLIED: bike -0.5121, bus -0.2301, ferry +0.6713, light rail +0.4143.
read_against_the_field_this_pass
Two published methods now bracket this project's loop and both were read this pass. (1) Chen, Prakash, Lima de Azevedo & Ben-Akiva (2020, TR-C 119:102650) names this project's coordinate descent for what it is: 'myopic heuristics in the sense that they do not consider the fundamental inter-dependencies among choice-models and do not have a systematic way to adjust model parameters' - and their non-myopic alternative calibrates precisely this project's target set at once (activity shares, mode shares, mode-specific OD flows, mode-specific sensor counts). (2) The WFRC/RSG ActivitySim framework publishes New ASC = Old ASC + ln(Target Proportion / Model Proportion) verbatim - the exact expression in asc_fixed_point.py - inside a CYCLIC protocol over model components, and states plainly that 'It is typically the case that not all calibration and validation targets can be achieved simultaneously.' | 2026-09-11 (third bracket): POLARIS's published procedure is the same cyclic ASC-by-purpose update, TIERED by iteration so that 'network state' can 'adapt to this change in demand' before the next tier is touched, with counts and speeds explicitly outside the calibrated set ('can only be minimally calibrated'). MATSim-NYC calibrated NO demand constants at all - its nested logit was estimated on RHTS + TLC/FHV/Citi Bike records and converted analytically - and spent its six SPSA iterations on twelve link-CAPACITY factors instead, which is the opposite allocation to this project's.

warm_start
--warm-start <dead run dir> exists in src/run/run_matsim.py: it resumes from a dead run's newest plans checkpoint and records warm_started_from; it is crash recovery, not a bit-identical continuation (positions/runs-and-economics.md). Checkpoints follow RUN.controler.write_plans_interval = 100 = the gate interval, so a death at iteration 98 has nothing past it.1 to resume from. This matches the platform's own answer (MATSim issue #834: restart AT the checkpoint iteration from its post-replanning plans) - the platform has no finer mechanism, and the interval is the whole trade.

    calibration_tooling
    Three named routes, all read this pass: (1) matsim.calibration in matsim-vsp/matsim-python-tools - an ASCCalibrator driving an Optuna study, whose update is literally log(z_i) - log(m_i) - (log(z_0) - log(m_0)), i.e. the classic ASC fixed-point loop normalised on a fixed reference mode, with a pluggable learning-rate scheduler and a TerminationCondition dataclass whose check_termination carries "# TODO: not used yet"; (2) Cadyts, a Bayesian count calibration that adjusts NO parameter and instead adds a utility bonus so agents select the plans matching observed counts; (3) opdyts (Flotterod, TR-B 2017), which approximates point equilibria of the mobsim/scoring/replanning loop, with a Berlin mode-constant example. See calibration_methods.

    2026-09-11
    restart_mechanism
    NO checkpoint/resume exists in the platform. The developer answer (Marcel Rieser, matsim-code-examples issue #834, 12 Dec 2022, read via api.github.com this pass): 'The plans in "it200/200.plans.xml.gz" are the plans after replanning, but before mobsim, in iteration 200. So you can use those to resume at iteration 200 (it should generate the same events file like the first run), and then continue with iteration 201.' and 'If you use the plans file of iteration 200, start the new run also with iteration 200.' ... 'The first iteration of a run never does replanning.' So a resume is a plans-file restart AT the checkpoint iteration, and only where a plans dump exists (writePlansInterval); everything since the last dump is lost. Memory rule of thumb from the same repository's issue #189: 'typically... around 100KB per agent. That is 1 GB per 10k agents' (mrieser, 2019-08-20); a ~1M-agent, 250k-link scenario needed 60-90 GB actual (mrieser); JVM total is ~25% above the reported heap (josiekre).

1E25Rail bonus: the submode preference for rail over bus at equal serviceOUTlight_rail -57.3 vs bus +44.8strong sign, moderate evidenceeverything; two switches built and offNEW ROW AND THE TOP MOVER. The literature's rail bonus is exactly the inversion on the board, and the router cannot express any preference: one marginalUtilityOfTraveling for all four submodes (9.162). C.raptor.mode_cost_representation = mode_constant or RUN.mode_choice.pt_submode_alternatives = alternatives puts the constants where the submode is chosen. Either opens a family; neither has been run.
2H10Choice-set coverage as a binding constraint on any constant or priceINride -41.0; pt submodes bounded by 25.78 %strongeverythingPARTIAL -> IN this pass: the board reading names ride's deficit a choice-set finding. Per the MATSim source the coverage is per executed TRIP, which makes the bound stricter, not looser. Only a generator moves ride - and 9.164's every_plan placement is that generator, unread on any result.
3E12Reliability and headwayPARTIALbus +44.8 vs light_rail -57.3strongeverything; measured spread, no seeded valueINERT -> PARTIAL: headway and reliability now reach scoring behind a switch that ships absent. Turning it on prices the half-hourly bus against the frequent tram for the first time; family boundary.
4F5Router-scorer consistency: does the search optimise the utility the plan is scored by?PARTIALlight_rail, heavy_rail, bus, ferrystrongeverythingThree consistency mechanisms exist and all ship off; 0.63 % of agents hold plans differing in submode, so the four pt deviations are decided where no declared value reaches.

The network member dies in the mobsim on one stop in six; that stop-link repair is a build, not a run.

verdict
The ratio is not the problem: 1,884 live hand-written lines (GOAL + board + brief + positions) is a reasonable surface for a 71,000-line model. The problem is that the record is 47 % of all documentation and grows ~230 lines a day (34 sections, 2,760 lines in 12 days), and the position pages - the layer meant to absorb it - are at their caps and are accreting instead of retiring: 18 of the previous report's 19 contradictions persist and 20 more were found, almost all superseded bullets left under 'What is open'. The append-only record serves the goal (no decision is ever lost, every section is indexed and 14-logged, and it is never read whole); the position pages as written do not, because they have become a second, unpruned log.
keep
  • GOAL.md
  • STATUS.md generated blocks + a hand-written Next/Open-work capped as now
  • run_families.json
  • DECISIONS.md exactly as it is (frozen, append-only, indexed) - nothing recorded is lost by any change below
  • positions/ What is built / What is measured / Refused (the current truth)
  • the generated reference and its --check gates
  • HANDOVER_CONTRACT.md as the ONE home for the reading rules
  • docs/reports/reference/ (the research library)
drop_or_merge
whatwhyloses
NEXT_AGENT_BRIEF.md §0 and §1§0 is re-derived by command (the digest prints machine, branch, PRs; issue_gate prints issues) and §1 duplicates STATUS Next; keep only §2 traps (the one thing with no other home) and §3 approvals as a 30-line pagenothing recorded - every §0/§1 fact has a command or a board row
the 'History' list on every position page (13 x ~15 lines)the record's topical index already lists the sections per topic; a grep gives the same listnothing

docs/reports/*.html from gitdated, frozen, prunable by their own README; 8.3 MB; not framework documentationnothing - the README rows stay and git history keeps the bytes
the record's hand-maintained topical index (lines 55-213) as hand-writtengenerate it from the section headings + 14 rows (title, date, issues) so an unindexed section cannot exist and the index cannot lagnothing - the hand-written 'Looking for' phrases can be kept as a seed file
add_one_thing
a machine-readable superseded_by map for the record (section -> superseding section), written by /handoff beside the 14 row, so 'pointed past' becomes a check instead of a banner - and the position pages can be verified to cite nothing that has a superseder
record_length_answer
16,053 lines / 1.27 MB, 165 sections, 47 % of all documentation. It serves the goal as an audit trail: every one of the 165 sections is indexed and 14-logged, the frozen boundary is stated in three places consistently, and no reader is asked to read it whole. It does not serve the goal as the thing the position pages are failing to summarise: the pages cannot retire text as fast as the record adds it, and the doc-shape check only sees new sections. The fix is on the pages and the check, not the record.

In-flight work seen in the tree

The tree was clean at 20ae4e9 when the lanes ran. This session's own edits — SKILL.md, the new render_report.py, and the two reference-library files the research lanes refreshed — are the change the report lands with.

Since the last report, and the report process itself

Against the 10 September report (4d1d1bc): of its 44 findings 6 closed, 6 changed, 32 still open at HEAD (code lane); of its 16 recommendations, the historian counts the series-wide totals below and lists 8 still open today — the raptor control arm, the replication band, the TfNSW request, score MSA at the cutoff, the car fixed cost, the objective's denominator, the trip-length target, and what check_hardcoding means by "reaches". The performance picture changed in one respect: "heap never binding" is now false. The field library moved 6 rows on verified material and added per-mode data-acquisition and physical-fidelity cells to every row; the factor library reused all 90 literature halves, added 3 rows and a per-mode data block, and re-read every status at HEAD (IN 44 · PARTIAL 34 · INERT 2 · ASC 1 · OUT 9 over the carried rows, four class changes with their commits).

The process verdict. Yes, to an unusual degree: 76 of 105 recommendations (72 %) are TAKEN, 26 OPEN, 2 OVERTAKEN, 1 REPEATED-only; 8 of the 13 PRs merged since 7 Sep carry a report's recommendations in their body, and the median recommendation landed within one day (#152 the morning of R1, #166 the night of R4, #176 the afternoon of R6). Of the 76 taken, 3 were refused after checking (the tram priority, the wall-time hash, the registry load), 1 was a do-not honoured, 2 are held by a recorded decision, 4 are built and unrun and 9 are partial.

Instruments and honesty, not the model: of the 76 taken, 39 are tooling/process (of 46 issued), 12 documents (of 13), 25 GOAL-aligned (of 46) - and of those 25, the ones that reach the mobsim or scoring (crowding, innovation cutoff, filter_modes, raptor constant, service quality, score MSA, passenger placement) are built behind gates and only two have ever run in an arm (crowding on F32, filter_modes on F31/F32). The population/demand lane (GOAL requirement 5: 11 recommendations, ten of them from R2) is 0 for 11; requirement 7 (inside 10 %) is 9 taken, 7 open, 1 overtaken - taken when the item is an instrument, open when it needs an arm.

Following the reports has not moved the goal count: modes inside 10 % at each report read 0, 0, 1, 0, 0, 1, 1, 0 (R0..R6) and the only RESULT in the series (9 Sep) reads 0 of 12. What moved is what the board says about itself: the count rung from −89.35 % to +16.30 % (a map, not the model), the objective from four folded numbers to twelve, the issue gate from a label to a measurement, the pricer from 31.5 h to a band that held, and the choice-set ceiling that says ride cannot be reached by any constant. Gates fired since the series began: F24, F25, F26, F28, F30 (cost), F31; one horizon (F32); one death (F33).

Wrong at three a day. R1 -> R2 -> R3 were 4.5 h and 5.7 h apart with one PR and no reading between them; R3 re-marked 118 of its 131 findings STILL OPEN and R4 104 of 138, while 125 findings ran in chains of two or more consecutive reports (23 in four or more, one in all six). The two sharp reports (R5: 75 findings, 20 re-reports; R6: 44, 4) each asked a question the previous one could not, and each followed a reading or a rebuild. Cost per report: 6 agents, 52-77 search calls, 0.78-1.75 MB lodged (8.17 MB for the six). A report per session is a cost; a report per reading - after an arm reaches a gate or its horizon, or after a family rebuild - is the instrument. Never two in a day.

Of the 76 taken, 3 were refused after checking (the tram priority, the wall-time hash, the registry load), 1 was a do-not honoured, 2 are held by a recorded decision, 4 are built and unrun and 9 are partial.
what_was_taken
Instruments and honesty, not the model: of the 76 taken, 39 are tooling/process (of 46 issued), 12 documents (of 13), 25 GOAL-aligned (of 46) - and of those 25, the ones that reach the mobsim or scoring (crowding, innovation cutoff, filter_modes, raptor constant, service quality, score MSA, passenger placement) are built behind gates and only two have ever run in an arm (crowding on F32, filter_modes on F31/F32). The population/demand lane (GOAL requirement 5: 11 recommendations, ten of them from R2) is 0 for 11; requirement 7 (inside 10 %) is 9 taken, 7 open, 1 overtaken - taken when the item is an instrument, open when it needs an arm.
scoreboard
Following the reports has not moved the goal count: modes inside 10 % at each report read 0, 0, 1, 0, 0, 1, 1, 0 (R0..R6) and the only RESULT in the series (9 Sep) reads 0 of 12. What moved is what the board says about itself: the count rung from −89.35 % to +16.30 % (a map, not the model), the objective from four folded numbers to twelve, the issue gate from a label to a measurement, the pricer from 31.5 h to a band that held, and the choice-set ceiling that says ride cannot be reached by any constant. Gates fired since the series began: F24, F25, F26, F28, F30 (cost), F31; one horizon (F32); one death (F33).
cadence
Wrong at three a day. R1 -> R2 -> R3 were 4.5 h and 5.7 h apart with one PR and no reading between them; R3 re-marked 118 of its 131 findings STILL OPEN and R4 104 of 138, while 125 findings ran in chains of two or more consecutive reports (23 in four or more, one in all six). The two sharp reports (R5: 75 findings, 20 re-reports; R6: 44, 4) each asked a question the previous one could not, and each followed a reading or a rebuild. Cost per report: 6 agents, 52-77 search calls, 0.78-1.75 MB lodged (8.17 MB for the six). A report per session is a cost; a report per reading - after an arm reaches a gate or its horizon, or after a family rebuild - is the instrument. Never two in a day.
this_report
Any re-issue of the eight rows in still_open_from_last is a repeat; the replication band would be its sixth, the TfNSW lodgement its fourth.

Recommendations, ranked

Ranked by what each would prevent or move × how cheap it is. A repeat tag marks one an earlier report already issued; the process audit counts them against this report too.

  1. Refuse a launch whose heap is below the registry's own rule, and print the heap beside the price.
    RUN.machine.xmx's description is a rule (9.6 GiB + 87 GiB × fraction) that nothing evaluates; arm 0 died on it after 20.9 h. A pricing probe cannot price heap.
    change: src/run/run_matsim.py launch path: parse the rule from the field (or declare it as two fields), compare, refuse; announce_cost prints heap. Add RUN.machine.gc_log = true to the arm overlays — observation-only, opens no family — so the next stall has a GC log. · guard: a unit test on the refusal; tests/check_launch_refusal.py
  2. A stall that kills: turn RUN.monitor.stall_s from an observation into a stop, hosted with the ceiling watcher.
    13.1 h of arm 0's 20.9 h were one iteration, with the machine awake and the digest reporting the stall at 05:13. The Task Scheduler log rules out sleep and scheduled jobs (this pass); the GC log is what remains.
    change: kill at ≥ 3 × the pace band's top (~760 s at 25 %) or a declared RUN.gate.stall_kill_s; write stopped_at_stall with the cause; make --detach the documented launch for an arm that outlives a session. · guard: tests/check_gate_watcher.py gains a stall case
  3. Fix the network build's four-value unpack and put the network build under a smoke test.
    build_matsim_network.py:137 cannot run since 25 Aug; the README says the package is regenerable from raw and it is not. 62 of 81 src/ modules are imported by no unit test.
    change: j, jar = tc.require(); a unit test that imports every builder and calls its java() helper against a stub. · guard: tests/unit import sweep over src/build and cities/<city>/build
  4. Route plan removal through the declared selector everywhere, or declare that EscortCoherenceListener.trim() is the removal. opens a family (Java)
    One of F33's five paired controls (RUN.replanning.plan_selector_for_removal = SelectRandom, #174) is partly unreachable: the listener drops the worst plan by its own rule when a proposal overfills memory.
    change: call MATSim's PlanSelector for removal from trim(), or remove trim() and let the framework's over-cap removal act. · guard: param_config.reach() cannot see this — a unit test on the listener with a fake selector
  5. Relaunch arm 0 on the corrected overlay, then the five paired arms in the decided order — and read coverage on both sides of every pair. repeat ×3 F33 is open; each control opens its own
    Every model-side control the last six reports asked for is built and none has run: score MSA, plan removal, raptor constant, service quality, submodes, plus the spent demand fix. The scoreboard cannot move until they do.
    change: f33_baseline_25pct.json at 40 g with gc_log on and a stall kill; then #172's order. ~19 h × 6 arms. · guard: the gate at 100/200/300; report_choice_set_coverage.py --trend on both arms
  6. One bootstrap: make src/ an importable package and give builders a @citysim.build.main decorator.
    238 sys.path lines in 122 files, 36 pasted path preambles, 31 pasted timing blocks, 26 import-time registry.load() calls — 650–900 lines of bootstrap, every script runnable only by path.
    change: pyproject.toml + pip install -e . (or one .pth), a decorator that starts the clock and resolves the registry lazily; delete the pasted blocks. · guard: python -m compileall, the unit suite, check_hardcoding --strict; byte-identical build outputs
  7. Field-level config groups and one controler helper. opens a family (Java recompile)
    18 ReflectiveConfigGroups are 3,336 lines of ~140 getter/setter pairs; the "one instance in two roles" module is pasted seven times in CitysimControler.assemble.
    change: public @Parameter @Comment fields keeping every checkConsistency; one installHandler(Class<T>, boolean); verify on a 1 % probe's output_config.xml. · guard: byte-equal emitted config; the recompile opens a family by rule, so batch it with the next Java change
  8. One reader for src/analyse/: an IterationReading that streams trips, legs and plans once.
    Nine readers each compose the run path, parse the record and stream the tables; report() parses trips twice; extract_metrics.py parses trips four times and legs twice; 60 duplicate file pairs across the tree.
    change: one streaming reading serving report, extract_metrics, measure_iteration_modes, iteration_trips, summarise_run; write _metrics.json and _fit.json through their schemas. · guard: byte-equal _metrics.json on the F32 result; the output schemas
  9. Give every registry field a stage (build / assemble / run) and refuse a run overlay on a build-time field.
    A.parking.search_min_max is baked at assembly; a run overlay records it as moved while executing the base. calibrate.py:111-133 already holds the stage table the resolver lacks.
    change: a stage key in the field schema; _check_values refuses a run-overlay key whose stage is not run; render_docs shows it. · guard: check_city.py --all, a unit test
  10. Retire superseded bullets on the position pages, and pin them. repeat ×2
    37 contradictions, 18 carried from the last report; 9 of 13 pages carry zero currency claims; the pages have become a second log.
    change: at /handoff, delete a "What is open" bullet whose issue is closed or whose figure the newest arm supersedes; add one doc_currency.json claim per page (the family stamp and one figure); the board's Decisions-required paragraph reads from the tracker. · guard: check_doc_currency.py --strict; a shape rule that a position page's What is open cites only open issues
  11. Lodge the TfNSW bespoke-table request: mode × age, trip-length distribution by mode, occupancy by purpose. repeat ×3
    TfNSW will not release HTS unit records but does supply bespoke tables (factor lane, sourced). #50's acquisition and the walk and ride diagnoses are one request away; three reports have asked.
    change: one email to opendataprogram@transport.nsw.gov.au with the cell list; record the lodgement on #50. · guard: #50 gets an AWAITING-DECISION line with a date
  12. Acquire the three open observations this pass found: BOAM bus occupancy, the Opal Patronage daily series (a candidate disclosed ferry count), BITRE registrations by postcode. a target change opens no family; a demand change would
    Ferry's target is DERIVED from a lockdown-month census cell because no patronage series was in the package; the field lane found the TfNSW hub carries per-service bus occupancy and daily tap-ons by mode and centre, both CC-BY.
    change: three fetch_* adapters with provenance; if Newcastle is a centre in the Opal series the ferry target becomes measured. · guard: check_manifest.py; the target's status column
  13. Declare the report cadence: one report per reading, not per session.
    Nine reports in eight days; R1→R2→R3 were 4.5 h and 5.7 h apart with no reading between; 125 findings ran in chains of two or more consecutive reports. 72 % of recommendations were taken and the goal count did not move, because what each report could add between readings was instruments.
    change: in SKILL.md: a pass runs after an arm reaches a gate or its horizon, after a family opens, or on request — and says which; the renderer makes a pass cheap when it does run. · guard: the README index's row states the reading the report followed
  14. Move the dated HTML reports out of git (keep the index and the reference library).
